claims.observation: GameOverScreen.OnEnter appends the deceased character with class/traits/age/kills/boss record, clears candidate branches, marks IsDead and resets run flags, Lich gains and the one-reroll flag. FreeEntrance and five challenge tokens survive where other special items are removed; death does not reset manor/equipment arrays or Gold in this observed boundary.

claims.observation: LoadCurrentBranches generates three candidates only when CurrentBranches is absent/empty, stores candidate class/spell/traits/age/portrait and saves Lineage; otherwise restores existing candidates. Candidate generation calls LineageObj with createEmpty=false. This prevents ordinary screen reopen from intentionally regenerating offers, subject to actual save success.

claims.observation: CreateRandomTraits reuses ONE inclusive 0..100 roll for both thresholds: first <94, second <55; so code-derived probability is 55/101 two traits, 39/101 one, 7/101 none. Rarity cutoffs are cumulative 48/85/100 with <= and inclusive RNG, yielding 49/101,37/101,15/101, rather than exactly 48/37/15 percent. Duplicate second traits and five incompatible pairs are rejected.

Health_Up is +10 per purchased level, base50/appreciation40/max75; every successful manor purchase increases global CurrentLevel, so even unrelated purchases raise later prices and can increase player HP/MP through level growth.

Navigation permits non-null visible skills; confirm checks enough gold and below MaxLevel and m_fadingIn=false, deducts gold then reveals manor/neighbor icons and increments skill/global level. paths.title: Catalog discovery, shop purchase/equip, rune consumers, spell casting, and durable state

claims.observation: A chest constructs candidates only from NotFound blueprints whose equipment level requirement and chest colour requirement are met. It randomly selects one, writes FoundButNotSeen, and opens the GetItem screen with its category/index. When all blueprint entries are already found, the chest falls back to gold or a stat drop.
claims.limits: Source inspection establishes candidate filtering and state assignment, not chest probabilities or live presentation behavior.

claims.observation: Blacksmith confirmation can purchase a found-but-not-purchased item if Gold covers EquipmentData.Cost; it deducts gold and marks the blueprint Purchased. The same confirmation can equip a purchased item if resulting CurrentWeight is at most MaxWeight, accounting for the currently equipped item's weight. Too-heavy equipment remains purchased but is not equipped. Existing equipped item can be unequipped.
claims.limits: Equipment stat aggregation is outside this note; screen code demonstrates equip-state mutation and the weight gate.

claims.observation: Enchantress confirmation purchases a found rune when Gold >= GetAbilityCost, subtracts that cost, marks it Purchased, and immediately equips it in that equipment category. The cost is integer(base ability cost + TotalRunesPurchased * 175); InitializeAbilityCosts assigns a base of 175 for the normal category/ability combinations. Later purchased runes can replace the rune in a category, or an equipped rune can be unequipped with -1. Thus the per-category equipped array limits the player to one rune of a given category at a time.
claims.limits: The flat 175 base applies to the initialized listed combinations; the array initializes unsupported combinations to 9999.

claims.observation: TotalDoubleJumps equals the count of equipped DoubleJump runes plus any equipment secondary DoubleJump attribute. During airborne jump input, PlayerObj accepts another jump only while m_doubleJumpCount < TotalDoubleJumps and the drop-through timer is nonpositive; it applies upward acceleration, increments the count, and plays the jump effect/sound. This connects a purchased/equipped rune to a concrete movement action rather than a display-only bonus.
claims.limits: This does not establish how the timing/feel behaves in a live run.

claims.observation: The PLAYER_SPELL1 input calls CastSpell(false) after the spell delay; SpellSword2 can call CastSpell(false, true) from the block input. CastSpell captures the selected spell, builds ProjectileData, sets damage to integer(TotalMagicDamage * spell damage multiplier), and calculates base mana as integer(base spell cost * (1 - Mana_Cost_Down modifier)). For Dagger the declared base cost is 10 and damage multiplier is 1. Before mega-cost scaling and before the final projectile gate, base-cost-sufficient mana allows Savant to change the next selected spell for non-Dragon/non-Traitor classes outside two carnival rooms; it chooses from the class spell list while excluding Translocator, TimeStop, and DamageShield. The current cast continues using the captured spellType. SpellSword mega-cast then multiplies cost, projectile scale, and damage by their respective modifiers. The projectile branch checks mana again and subtracts mana only after firing. Ambilevous inverts projectile SourceAnchor.X except for Bounce and DamageShield.

paths.title: Generated regions, optional timed fairy objective, and boss-clear aftermath

claims.observation: Boss-bearing sequential areas sample the room count with RandomInt((int)TotalRooms.X,(int)TotalRooms.Y), then retry area construction until size and EntranceBoss conditions pass. Each attempt increments creationCounter; creationCounter > 15 jumps to restartAll. Separately, missing top/bottom/right exits jumps to restartSequential.
claims.limits: The sequential retry counter increments after each boss-entrance attempt; the safety log text says non-sequential even in the sequential branch. Exit-layout failure restarts the area through a separate label.

claims.observation: A template room named Boss is replaced by a concrete boss-room object selected by its numeric Tag. Room properties and objects are copied and linked rooms are relinked when present.
claims.limits: Unknown tags leave the template unchanged; room assets/templates are outside this source span.

claims.observation: An Eyeball miniboss kill sets persistent EyeballBossBeaten when the target player remains alive. The boss-room base cleanup also sets per-hero NewBossBeaten. When the player later returns to CastleEntranceRoomObj, LastBossDoorHack opens the final door only if all four region boss flags are true and FinalDoorOpened is false. PlayerData writes and reads the four regional flags; MapData separately stores room visitation, bonus completion/IDs, chest type/open state, fairy failure, ordinary enemy deaths and breakables.
claims.limits: EyeballBossBeaten is a player-wide progression flag written to PlayerData, while NewBossBeaten marks the current heir and is consumed/reset by GameOver. MapData restores only the listed world-map state; boss room/chests and challenge rooms are excluded from relevant arrays, and enemy revival/retention depends on LockCastle.

claims.observation: Fairy chest condition state is checked by FairyChestObj.Draw while locked. For ReachIn5Seconds, the timer counts down during unpaused play; the checker fails it when the player remains farther than 100 units after timer reaches zero, or unlocks it when within 100 units while time remains. TakeNoDamage fails when PlayerObj.State is HURT, otherwise unlocks upon reaching within 100 units. Unlock reports ObjectiveComplete for ordinary conditions; failure reports ObjectiveFailed unless skipped. Opening a free chest marks a missing rune FoundButNotSeen, or grants a stat drop when all runes have been found.
claims.limits: ChestConditionChecker runs from Draw only while locked; drawing/caller timing is code-driven. MapData persists failed state as a boolean, not the detailed condition/timer state. Some objective conditions can be changed by proximity/order and are not all enumerated here.

trace.caller: LevelBuilder2.CreateLevel assembles rooms and converts boss templates; ProceduralLevelScreen handles room entry, boss doors, and room-entry saves. FairyChestObj.Draw calls ChestConditionChecker.SetConditionState while locked.
trace.gates: Boss-bearing area requires EntranceBoss and valid exits; safety counter is >15 before whole-map restart. Timed fairy condition is proximity <100 before timer expires; TakeNoDamage requires no HURT state before proximity <100. Boss final-door gate requires all four region flags and FinalDoorOpened false.
trace.costs: No currency cost shown; the player incurs traversal/time/health risk and some fairy objectives impose conditions or timers.
trace.mutations: Cloned room lists, boss-room replacement/link mutation, rune inventory state, NewBossBeaten, boss door lock state.
trace.consumers: Minimap, room traversal, boss chest/teleport, challenge access, rune inventory and item screen, SaveManager.
trace.failure_boundaries: Area retries; non-sequential creation has a 15-attempt map restart; missing linker triggers restartAll. Fairy objective can fail. A beaten-region boss door can lock and challenge access remains separate.
trace.persistence: PlayerData explicitly serializes the four regional boss flags. MapData serializes visited rooms, bonus completion/IDs, chest types/open booleans, fairy failure booleans, ordinary enemy dead booleans, and breakable booleans; corresponding loader restores them. Boss/challenge rooms are omitted from certain chest/enemy arrays. Ordinary enemies are silently killed on restore only when LockCastle is false; fairy failure restores under that same no-lock condition. Timer duration and objective completion states are not saved as such.

paths.title: ShieldKnight spacing, shield-facing defense, player block/damage, kill or death aftermath

claims.observation: EnemyObj.Update maps configured radii into four range states and, once active logic/cooldown permit, dispatches by difficulty. ShieldKnight InitializeLogic creates stop/walk/turn sets; basic/advanced use the basic logic block, expert uses an expert turn set, and engaged states turn when heading disagrees with target position or walk toward the target otherwise. Miniboss logic always chooses stop in these three states.
claims.limits: This is a movement/turn loop, not a melee/projectile attack set. Specific attack behavior is not present for this ShieldKnight implementation excerpt.

claims.observation: ShieldKnight CollisionResponse has a guard requiring a PlayerObj (`player != null`) as well as front-side position, first-box-hit, and applicable invulnerability. Its additional guard excludes the PlayerAirAttack sprite. Thus a pure projectile cannot enter this branch, despite a nested projectile-destroy block. Eligible front player contact runs the shield response and specific knockback. HitEnemy reduction is separate: code tests current m_target position and current m_target.SpriteName, not the actual attacker/source or isPlayer; despite the nearby comment, qualifying calls can include non-sword damage if those current-target tests pass. The scalar is 0.6, so the applied formula is `(int)(damage * (1 - 0.6))`.
claims.limits: Comment at lines 416-417 says air attacks and all other damage besides sword swipes should deal full damage, but executable check is target sprite name only. The nested projectile destruction is structurally present but excluded for ordinary pure projectile inputs by the outer player != null guard.

claims.observation: Player block absorbs eligible collisions while blocking and when mana is positive or block invulnerability remains; each hit outside that window drains BlockManaDrain and starts BlockInvincibleTime. Otherwise HitPlayer computes mitigated damage, sets computed damage to zero before tutorial completion, and subtracts it from health only when GodMode is false. The mana gate is positive mana, not necessarily enough for the full BlockManaDrain. Lethal damage may consume Revive, pass a Death_Dodge roll, eject the player from a challenge boss room, or kill and run game over.
claims.limits: Death_Dodge probability is configured by a skill modifier whose bought value is not traced.

claims.observation: Enemy kill may grant vampirism/mana and drops, records current room/enemy index in EnemiesKilledInRun when SaveToFile is true, increments total and type/difficulty kill counters, then enters base killed state. The room lookup throws if that enemy cannot be found.
claims.limits: Drop rates and class-specific gains depend on values outside this excerpt; no runtime play observed.

trace.caller: ProceduralLevelScreen updates attached enemies; EnemyObj.Update selects range state and AI logic; collision dispatch reaches ShieldKnight or PlayerObj response.
trace.gates: Shield response outer guard requires first-box hit, appropriate invulnerability state, front-facing collision, and player != null; air-attack sprite is excluded. This makes the nested projectile destruction unreachable for an ordinary projectile-only collision. Player damage mitigation instead checks player block state/resource.
trace.costs: Block costs BlockManaDrain mana on eligible hits outside invulnerability; unblocked hits cost computed health. Enemy tuning varies by difficulty.
trace.mutations: Shield collision produces player-specific knockback and enemy invulnerability; the nested projectile-destroy code exists but is unreachable for pure projectile input due to the player guard. HitEnemy damage factor uses target position/sprite checks, not attacker identity.
trace.consumers: Enemy HUD, item drop manager, vampirism/mana systems, current run map, kill counters, death-defy/game-over flow.
trace.failure_boundaries: Shield front branch requires player; pure projectile cannot enter it. HitEnemy comment claims sword-swipe semantics, while actual test uses m_target current sprite and facing. Tutorial/GodMode suppress player damage; Revive and Death_Dodge intercept lethal outcomes; challenge boss lethal hit ejects instead of ordinary death; missing enemy lookup throws.
trace.persistence: Enemy kill updates PlayerStats.EnemiesKilledInRun; room entry saves PlayerData/MapData. Exact serialization and kill-time durability are not traced.

cross_path_loop: Death record -> three frozen legal builds (pool depends on retained manor) -> selected class/traits/spell + purchased/equipped gear/runes -> conditional rooms/objectives/combat -> actual gold/discovery/boss/history aftermath -> retained investments and next offers

yair_observations.observation: Body records already distinguish inherited Natural balance, trained Conditioned grip and acquired Palm mark. Awakening/activation is paid elapsed-time work, grip practice has stamina/soreness cost, and ordinary recovery preserves permanent marks/learned grip. Active balance contributes route preparation; grip changes actual packing duration and tender hands add work time. No general trait framework is missing.

Existing sluice material/frame responses already require recovered hands and Strength8. The inspected action list has no specific sure-footing response consuming awakened Natural balance and Conditioned grip together. That is a narrow authored consumer candidate, not a claim that traits lack functional effects.

Field renewal already previews losses, returns only Load-bearing Step mastery to1, reopens its practice, zeroes focus/drive reserve and strain, and retains native inventory/equipment/XP/people/workshop. Campaign transition planners require safe boundaries and support explicit reset domains; they do not establish a complete selectable heir/death lifecycle. Chronicle old age explicitly ends the chosen life once.

Helper commission already pays three coins and transfers one log, spawns a durable simulation actor, uses a funded local controller and returns one actual kit for collection. prepareSimulationEffects freezes the spawn template and derived unique identity in the command job. The inspected hire command chooses one template; it does not present a saved set of three distinct candidate builds before contracting.

persistExpansionPlan writes staged expansion/native money, gameplay/ownership/equipment/unlocks and optional native projection into the existing copied envelope before storage.setItem. prepareGameplayPublication stages item reconstruction and XP, refusing negative XP without a reset adapter. A new proposal must use this publisher and its matching live host, not Rogue Legacy separate-file/catch-only persistence. Source reading alone does not verify failure atomicity in play.

Site project compiler checks phase dependencies/cycles and compiles paid participant jobs into retained world phase facts. Current dry rack and fitting shelf already provide permanent useful upgrade consumers. Another generic manor/upgrade ledger is unnecessary without a new concrete consumer.

yair_worker_mappings.reuse: Native equipment and inventory remain owned by their current player/NPC owners. The sluice already makes Nera's actually owned/equipped field frame alter defense/blocking and Oren's actual equipped hook pole enable hook-specific stamina/guard effects. Feature-object fitting knives are conserved, custody-checked hand tools and explicitly not equipment bonuses. These are useful precedents for functional gear, but there is no player kit choice inside this encounter.
yair_worker_mappings.narrow_candidate: As a reversible original encounter proposal, let the player prepare one of two real carried kits before admission: a lighter traversal kit that changes an escape affordance, or a braced kit that changes a guard affordance. Reuse actual inventory/equipment custody and fighter snapshots; do not make either a flat stat reward.
yair_worker_mappings.missing_consumer: featureBattleView and commitFeatureBattleAction expose combat/objective actions but no player kit-selection action or kit-specific player behavior; the current gear-derived special case is authored for the NPC frame/pole. Do not call fitting knives missing gear; they already have separate tool consumers.
yair_worker_mappings.retention: Prefer existing player inventory/equipment as durable ownership and put only encounter-local choice/effect receipts into a separately versioned nativeBattle payload. Keep prior battle schemas frozen; explicit compatibility decision and save/reload verification would be required before persistence changes.
yair_worker_mappings.later_gate: Rebuild and exercise both choices in a browser: verify each changes its declared action result, switching/withdrawal conserves ownership, and a save/reload resumes the same admitted choice.

yair_worker_mappings.reuse: Optional conduct/prepared challenges already require explicit enrollment, bind actual battle IDs/results and preserve finite attempt histories. Feats retain committed receipts. A successful sluice passage earns the existing one-time Combat XP and route fact; current challenge descriptions explicitly promise recognition only and no repeat payment. The refreshed root now also validates an optional fieldcraft record; this additive integration does not change the cited attempt settlement or recognition-only reward boundary.
yair_worker_mappings.narrow_candidate: A separate opt-in challenge can ask for one additional declared objective condition and grant one finite, concrete workshop material only on its first qualified receipt. Keep ordinary victory/objective settlement and existing no-strike/prepared recognition unchanged; the material payout is a proposal, not an existing reward.
yair_worker_mappings.missing_consumer: The current challenge root retains result/admission/violation receipts and feat recognition, but has no challenge-owned reward claim or consumer. finish has one common success payout, not a challenge-specific material award. The already-implemented no-strike, prepared-team, and objective-completion gates are not gaps. The new fieldcraft validator/feats integration is separate and does not add a challenge payout.
yair_worker_mappings.retention: Derive eligibility from the settled attempt receipt; persist an idempotent claim in the optional character record and grant through existing item/effect owners. Need optional enrollment/old-save absence behavior and an explicit schema compatibility decision if fields are added.
yair_worker_mappings.later_gate: Browser acceptance: decline enrollment with no change; complete the declared objective once and receive one real item; repeat/failed/withdrawn attempts cannot pay again; save/reload preserves receipt and claim.

yair_worker_mappings.reuse: This proposed mechanic is already implemented for explicitly enrolled schema-4 sluice sessions: an actual defended strike earns a saved next-player-choice window against its actual attacker; retreat and counter are distinct paid actions, any other choice expires it, enemy cadence continues, and receipts validate the defended origin. Do not report this as missing from the current feature encounter.
yair_worker_mappings.narrow_candidate: Reuse the current defended-next-choice contract for one explicitly enrolled original encounter with a different authored enemy trigger or counter consequence, only if play review shows a distinct context adds value. Otherwise keep the current sluice as the complete local proof.
yair_worker_mappings.missing_consumer: The bounded native road duel remains a schema-1 automatic strike/withdraw exchange; its host has no such counter-window consumer. The feature sluice owns this effect only in its opted-in schema-4 path, while frozen schema-3 behavior stays separate.
